messages.body_plain:
The figures didn't show up.

See the end of chapter 7 of the R/qtl book for a discussion of cim(), https://rqtl.org/book. The implementation in R/qtl is rather crude. It fills in any missing data at the markers and then uses forward selection to n.marcovar markers to pick the covariates.

Personally, I prefer stepwiseqtl().

I'm not sure that there is a way to know how many markers to use.

If I saw a single large QTL in scanone(), I might include its genotype as a covariate in a second call to scanone(). Alternatively, you can use makeqtl() and then addqtl(). See Ch 9 of the R/qtl book.

karl

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] confidence interval
messages.body_plain:
lodint() and bayesint(), for scanone() output, assume one QTL on a chromosome.

If you want to consider multiple QTL on a chromosome, it's probably best to fit a two-qtl model and derive confidence intervals from that.

Using makeqtl() to create a QTL object including your two QTLs.
Use refineqtl() to revise the QTL locations.
Pass the output of refineqtl() to lodint().

karl

  QTL_Leaf$pheno[,2] <- as.numeric(QTL_Leaf$pheno[,2])

The QTL_Leaf object is a list with one component named "pheno". That component is a data frame and you want the second column to be numeric.

Note I don't think you can have an object named "QTL_Leaf-first-rep" because "-" isn't allowed within an object name.

But I would maybe look at your original data file to see what is in that column that is coming out as non-numeric, and maybe fix the problem there.

karl
